high.title: Hardcoded symmetric key in ResetPasswordActivity
high.description: The app uses a hardcoded symmetric key ('0123456789!@#$%^') to encrypt and decrypt password reset tokens. An attacker with access to the APK can recover this key and decrypt any intercepted tokens or forge valid tokens for any email address.
high.impact: Anything the app encrypts with it can be decrypted, and forged, by anyone holding the APK.

low.title: Exported activity NewPasswordActivity has no permission protection
low.description: Activity "edu.ksu.cs.benign.NewPasswordActivity" is reachable by any app on the device (Has an intent-filter and no explicit android:exported (implicitly exported)) and declares no permission. It handles NEWPASS. NewPasswordActivity is exported via an intent-filter without any permission guards. It processes 'initVector' and 'generatedToken' extras to decrypt and display a user's email address. Because it uses a hardcoded key, any application on the device can use this activity as a decryption oracle to recover emails from intercepted tokens. The exported activity NewPasswordActivity does not verify the presence of the 'initVector' intent extra. If the extra is missing, Base64.decode returns null, and the subsequent instantiation of IvParameterSpec throws a NullPointerException, crashing the app.
low.impact: A malicious application on the same device can crash the app by sending an intent to the exported NewPasswordActivity without the required extras.
low.recommendation: Set android:exported="false" if it is internal, or guard it with a signature-level permission and validate all input.

reasons: The decryption oracle provides no gain over the hardcoded key in The app uses a hardcoded symmetric key..., and the missing extra only results in a crash.

info.title: Lack of screenshot protection on sensitive screens
info.description: The application does not set FLAG_SECURE on activities that handle sensitive password reset tokens and user emails, allowing screenshots and screen recordings of this data.
info.impact: Sensitive information displayed during the password reset process can be captured by other apps or the user.
info.recommendation: Set WindowManager.LayoutParams.FLAG_SECURE in the onCreate method of sensitive activities.

reasons: Screen contents not protected from capture. Without FLAG_SECURE, what a screen shows can end up in screenshots, screen recordings and the task-switcher preview. That matters on screens showing credentials, card numbers or balances; on its own it is a hardening note.

info.title: No network security config declared
info.description: The app declares neither android:networkSecurityConfig nor usesCleartextTraffic, so it relies on platform defaults and pins no domain. With targetSdkVersion 27 those defaults still permit cleartext HTTP (see the cleartext finding).
info.impact: Without pinning, anyone who gets a CA trusted on the device can read and alter the app's TLS traffic.
info.recommendation: Declare a network security config that disables cleartext and pins the domains that carry sensitive traffic.

reasons: No certificate pinning. Pinning defends against an attacker who already controls a trusted CA or the device's trust store. Without one of those, TLS is still doing its job. It becomes a finding when paired with what the unpinned channel actually carries.
Lack of pinning is a hardening note and does not provide a concrete gain without a compromised CA or device trust store.

info.title: Task hijacking (StrandHogg) possible on Android 10 and lower
info.description: minSdkVersion 22 lets the app run on Android versions before 11, and its task affinity is its package name "edu.ksu.cs.benign". There, another app can declare the same affinity, with allowTaskReparenting, and have its own activity shown in this app's task. The app targets SDK 27 and uses the default taskAffinity (the package name) for its activities, including sensitive password reset screens.
info.impact: On Android 10 and lower, a malicious app declaring the same taskAffinity can hijack the task and overlay a fraudulent UI to steal user credentials during the password reset process.
info.recommendation: Raise minSdkVersion to 30, where Android fixed this. Until then, android:taskAffinity="" on the <application> mitigates the original attack, though not its runtime variant on unpatched Android 9 and lower.
